name: Extra Time
subject: Sport
tagline: Twenty questions from the pitch, the court and the track. Starts easy, ends hard.

questions.q: How many players from each team are on the pitch at the start of a football match?
questions.w: Eleven a side, including the goalkeeper.
questions.more: The number was fixed in the 1860s when English public schools wrote the first common rules. Substitutes were not allowed in top-level matches until the 1960s, so an injured player simply left his team a man short.

questions.q: Which country has won the most men's FIFA World Cups?
questions.more: Brazil is also the only country to have played in every tournament since the first in 1930. Germany and Italy follow with four each.

questions.q: In tennis, what word is used for a score of zero?
questions.w: Love. Forty-love means one player has no points in the game.
questions.more: The most popular explanation is that it comes from playing for love, meaning for nothing. Another traces it to l'oeuf, French for egg, for the shape of a zero, much like a duck in cricket.

questions.q: How many years are there between one Summer Olympics and the next?
questions.w: Four. The gap is called an Olympiad.
questions.more: The Winter Games were held in the same year until 1992, then shifted to sit two years apart, so some form of Olympics now comes round every two years. The modern Games have only been cancelled by war.

questions.q: Which sport is played with a shuttlecock?
questions.w: Badminton. The shuttlecock's feathered skirt makes it slow sharply in flight.
questions.more: Off the racket a shuttlecock is the fastest object in any sport, recorded at over 490 kilometres an hour, but drag kills that speed within metres. The game takes its name from Badminton House in Gloucestershire.

questions.q: True or false: a marathon is 26.2 miles long.
questions.w: True. That is 42.195 kilometres.
questions.more: The odd number comes from the 1908 London Games, where the course was extended so it could start at Windsor Castle and finish in front of the royal box. It was fixed as the official distance in 1921.

questions.q: In basketball, how many points is a shot from beyond the arc worth?
questions.w: Three. Inside the arc it is two, and a free throw is one.
questions.more: The three-point line only arrived in the NBA in 1979 and was treated as a gimmick at first. Teams now take more than ten times as many of them per game as they did in the 1980s.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics?
questions.w: Rio de Janeiro, the first Olympics held in South America.
questions.more: Tokyo followed in 2021 after a year's delay, then Paris in 2024. Los Angeles hosts in 2028 and Brisbane in 2032.

questions.q: What is Usain Bolt's world record for the 100 metres?
questions.w: 9.58 seconds, set in Berlin in 2009.
questions.more: He had broken his own record twice in the previous year. His top speed in that race was about 44 kilometres an hour, and no one has come within a tenth of a second of the mark since.

questions.q: How many players are in a cricket team?
questions.w: Eleven, the same as football.
questions.more: A twelfth man can field as a substitute but may not bat or bowl. Cricket and football settled on eleven independently in nineteenth-century England, which is probably coincidence rather than design.

questions.q: Which tennis Grand Slam is played on clay?
questions.w: The French Open at Roland Garros. Wimbledon is grass, and the other two are hard courts.
questions.more: Clay slows the ball and makes it bounce high, rewarding patience over power. Rafael Nadal won there fourteen times, a record of dominance at a single event that is unmatched anywhere in the sport.

questions.q: What colour is the jersey worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France?
questions.w: Yellow, the maillot jaune. Green is for points and polka dots for the mountains.
questions.more: Yellow was chosen because the newspaper that founded the race, L'Auto, was printed on yellow paper. The jersey was introduced in 1919, sixteen years after the first Tour.

questions.q: In golf, what is a score of one under par on a hole called?
questions.w: A birdie. Two under is an eagle, three under an albatross, and one over is a bogey.
questions.more: Birdie comes from American slang around 1900, where a bird of a shot meant an excellent one. The bigger birds were added later to keep the theme going as the scores got better.

questions.q: Judo originated in which country?
questions.w: Japan. Jigoro Kano founded it in 1882.
questions.more: Kano stripped the most dangerous techniques out of older jujutsu schools so it could be practised at full effort safely. It became the first Asian martial art in the Olympics, at Tokyo in 1964.

questions.q: Select every sport that was on the programme at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
questions.w: Breaking, surfing and skateboarding were all in Paris. Squash was not; it joins the programme in Los Angeles in 2028.
questions.more: Breaking appeared only once, as hosts may propose sports for their own Games. Paris held its surfing event in Tahiti, nearly 16,000 kilometres from the host city.

questions.q: Put these competitions in order of when they were first held, earliest first.
questions.w: Wimbledon in 1877, the modern Olympics in 1896, the Tour de France in 1903 and the World Cup in 1930.
questions.more: The Tour was invented to sell newspapers during a circulation war, and the first World Cup was played in Uruguay with just thirteen teams, several of whom crossed the Atlantic by boat together.

questions.q: Which athlete has won the most Olympic gold medals?
questions.w: Michael Phelps, with 23 golds and 28 medals in total across four Games.
questions.more: Eight of those golds came at Beijing in 2008, a single-Games record. Swimming offers many events at similar distances and strokes, which is why swimmers dominate these lists.

questions.q: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.w: Uruguay, who hosted it and beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.
questions.more: Uruguay were given the tournament partly because they had won the previous two Olympic football titles and were marking a century of independence. Only four European teams made the long trip.

questions.q: In rugby union, how many points is a try worth?
questions.w: Five, with a conversion kick worth two more.
questions.more: A try was originally worth nothing at all. It merely earned the chance to try a kick at goal, which is where the name comes from, and its value has been raised repeatedly to encourage attacking play.

questions.q: Which is the oldest of the four tennis Grand Slam tournaments?
questions.w: Wimbledon, first played in 1877. The US Open followed in 1881.
questions.more: That first Wimbledon had one event, men's singles, and 22 entrants. The final was delayed by rain, a tradition the tournament has kept up ever since.
